method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Trauma - primary survey' (Last Updated January 2022), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **Before arrival:** activate the trauma team, brief the team on the anticipated injuries and priorities, **estimate the child's weight** and prepare age- and weight-appropriate doses and equipment.
claims.source_text: Activate trauma team and/or advise relevant personnel (eg radiographer and blood bank) … Conduct a pre-arrival briefing for team with a verbal synthesis of the anticipated injuries and management priorities … Estimate the child’s weight … Prepare age/weight appropriate doses of medication and equipment
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - primary survey' (Last Updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Major_paediatric_trauma_The_primary_survey/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Take a 'hands-off' ambulance handover** unless a life threat needs immediate action, then perform the primary survey. A dedicated staff member should support the family.
claims.source_text: Obtain handover from ambulance staff (unless there is a life threat requiring immediate action) - ‘hands-off’ … Perform primary survey … Ensure a dedicated member of staff is available to provide support for the family
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - primary survey' (Last Updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Major_paediatric_trauma_The_primary_survey/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Priorities, assessed and managed in parallel:** catastrophic haemorrhage · airway with c-spine control · breathing · circulation · disability · exposure/environment.
claims.source_text: Priorities are the parallel assessment and management of: < c > Catastrophic haemorrhage A Airway (with c-spine control) B Breathing C Circulation D Disability E Exposure / Environment
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - primary survey' (Last Updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Major_paediatric_trauma_The_primary_survey/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Controlling exsanguinating external haemorrhage comes first.** Apply direct pressure with a gauze pad; **use a tourniquet for life-threatening limb haemorrhage.**
claims.source_text: Control of exsanguinating external haemorrhage is the first priority … Apply direct pressure to the wound with a gauze pad … Use a tourniquet to control life-threatening limb haemorrhage
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - primary survey' (Last Updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Major_paediatric_trauma_The_primary_survey/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Leave bandages that control significant bleeding in place** until the child is stable and IV access is secured. Don't use layers of gauze that absorb and hide blood loss.
claims.source_text: Bandages controlling significant bleeding should not be removed until the child is stable and IV access is secured … Do not use layers of gauze/bandages that may absorb and conceal blood loss
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - primary survey' (Last Updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Major_paediatric_trauma_The_primary_survey/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Apply a pelvic binder if a pelvic fracture is suspected and there is haemodynamic compromise**; activate the massive transfusion protocol if appropriate.
claims.source_text: Apply a pelvic binder if a pelvic fracture is suspected and there is haemodynamic compromise … Activate the hospital massive transfusion protocol if appropriate
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - primary survey' (Last Updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Major_paediatric_trauma_The_primary_survey/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Assess the airway, anterior neck and conscious level (AVPU)**; look for facial fractures and blood, vomit or loose teeth in the airway.
claims.source_text: Assess airway, anterior neck and level of consciousness (using AVPU) … Look for evidence of facial fractures, blood/vomit/loose teeth in airway
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - primary survey' (Last Updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Major_paediatric_trauma_The_primary_survey/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Burns — look for airway involvement:** singed facial or nasal hair, facial burns, hoarse voice, harsh cough, head or neck swelling, soot in the mouth, nose or saliva.
claims.source_text: If burns present, assess for: Singeing of facial / nasal hair Facial burns Hoarseness of voice Harsh cough Head or neck swelling Soot in mouth, nose or saliva
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - primary survey' (Last Updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Major_paediatric_trauma_The_primary_survey/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Use an age-appropriate neutral head position** — under 8 years, a thoracic elevation device or a towel under the shoulder blades.
claims.source_text: Use an age appropriate neutral head position … Use a thoracic elevation device or towel under shoulder blades to achieve this if <8 years old
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - primary survey' (Last Updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Major_paediatric_trauma_The_primary_survey/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Every spontaneously breathing patient gets high-flow oxygen** (typically 10–15 L via non-rebreather mask), whatever the need for airway support.
claims.source_text: Regardless of the need for airway support, all spontaneously breathing patients should have high-flow oxygen applied (typically 10-15 L via non-rebreather mask)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - primary survey' (Last Updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Major_paediatric_trauma_The_primary_survey/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Airway support:** jaw thrust (no head-tilt or chin lift), gentle suction, an oropharyngeal airway if tolerated or a nasopharyngeal airway if base-of-skull fracture is unlikely, and endotracheal intubation.
claims.source_text: Support the airway if needed using the following techniques: Jaw thrust (avoiding head-tilt or chin lift) Gentle suction of airway to remove blood/vomitus/secretions Oropharyngeal airway if tolerated, or nasopharyngeal airway (if base of skull fracture unlikely) Endotracheal intubation
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - primary survey' (Last Updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Major_paediatric_trauma_The_primary_survey/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Protect the cervical spine with manual in-line stabilisation until a soft foam collar is applied.**
claims.source_text: Cervical spine should be protected with manual in-line stabilisation until a soft foam collar is applied
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - primary survey' (Last Updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Major_paediatric_trauma_The_primary_survey/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Breathing life threats to find and treat:** tension pneumothorax, open pneumothorax, massive haemothorax, flail chest, tracheo-bronchial injury.
claims.source_text: The life threats to identify and manage with regards to breathing include: Tension pneumothorax Open pneumothorax Massive haemothorax Flail chest Tracheo-bronchial injury
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - primary survey' (Last Updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Major_paediatric_trauma_The_primary_survey/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Tension pneumothorax: chest decompression with a finger or instrument, thoracostomy or intercostal catheter.** Needle decompression may be used in emergencies but is unlikely to work.
claims.source_text: Tension pneumothorax: chest decompression with a finger or instrument, thoracostomy or intercostal catheter insertion. Needle decompression may be used in emergencies but is unlikely to be effective
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - primary survey' (Last Updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Major_paediatric_trauma_The_primary_survey/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Open pneumothorax:** close it immediately and insert a chest drain. **Massive haemothorax:** chest drain and blood transfusion. **Flail chest:** analgesia; consider positive pressure ventilation.
claims.source_text: Open pneumothorax: immediate closure and chest drain insertion … Massive haemothorax: Chest drain insertion and blood transfusion … Flail chest: analgesia, consider positive pressure ventilation
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - primary survey' (Last Updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Major_paediatric_trauma_The_primary_survey/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Request a portable chest X-ray.** In intubated children, **insert an orogastric tube** so gastric dilatation doesn't impair ventilation.
claims.source_text: Request a portable chest X-Ray … In intubated children, insert an orogastric tube to prevent gastric dilatation which can impair effective ventilation
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - primary survey' (Last Updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Major_paediatric_trauma_The_primary_survey/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hunt for bleeding:** external (don't remove penetrating foreign bodies), intra-thoracic, intra-abdominal, intra-pelvic, long bones (particularly femoral), retroperitoneal, and scalp or intracranial in infants.
claims.source_text: sites of potential bleeding such as: External bleeding (expose wounds, do not remove penetrating foreign bodies) Intra-thoracic bleeding (assess for massive haemothorax) Intra-abdominal bleeding (inspect for distension, bruising. Palpate for tenderness) Intra-pelvic bleeding – secondary to a pelvic fracture (assess by gentle palpation of pelvic structures) Long bone fractures (particularly femoral) Retroperitoneal bleeding (degree of suspicion should remain high if no other obvious source for bleeding) Scalp or Intracranial bleeding in infants
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - primary survey' (Last Updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Major_paediatric_trauma_The_primary_survey/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **eFAST has a limited role in paediatric trauma.** Actively exclude obstructive shock (tension pneumothorax, cardiac tamponade) and neurogenic shock (spinal injury above T6).
claims.source_text: eFAST has a limited role in paediatric trauma … Care should also be taken to actively look for and exclude: Obstructive cause for shock (eg tension pneumothorax or cardiac tamponade) Neurogenic shock (associated with spinal injury above T6)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - primary survey' (Last Updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Major_paediatric_trauma_The_primary_survey/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Two IV cannulae, as large as practicable, ideally one in each cubital fossa**; send cross-match, FBE, VBG, LFTs, UEC, lipase and coagulation screen. **If IV access isn't rapid, go IO** into a non-injured leg or the humerus.
claims.source_text: Establish IV access with two cannulae that are as large as practicable, ideally one in each cubital fossa. Take blood for cross-match, FBE, VBG, LFTs, UEC, lipase, coagulation screen … If an IV cannula cannot be inserted rapidly, obtain IO access into a non-traumatised leg or humerus
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - primary survey' (Last Updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Major_paediatric_trauma_The_primary_survey/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Inadequate circulation: 10 mL/kg bolus of sodium chloride 0.9%.** Ongoing visible or suspected occult bleeding: **packed red cells 10 mL/kg** if available.
claims.source_text: If the circulation is inadequate, give 10 mL/kg bolus of sodium chloride 0.9%. … If there is ongoing visible bleeding or suspicion of occult bleeding give packed red blood cells (10 mL/kg) if available.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - primary survey' (Last Updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Major_paediatric_trauma_The_primary_survey/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Tranexamic acid 15 mg/kg** if there is haemodynamic compromise from suspected haemorrhage.
claims.source_text: Give Tranexamic Acid 15 mg/kg if there is haemodynamic compromise from suspected haemorrhage
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - primary survey' (Last Updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Major_paediatric_trauma_The_primary_survey/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Life-threatening abdominal, pelvic or retroperitoneal bleeding may need surgery or interventional radiology — consult early.** Uncontrollable bleeding may need theatre before the secondary survey is finished; a chest drain in massive haemothorax may help ventilation but only theatre stops the bleeding.
claims.source_text: Life threatening bleeding into the abdomen, pelvis or retroperitoneal space may require surgery or interventional radiology. Early consultation with paediatric surgery +/- interventional radiology is required. … Rapid transit to theatre, prior to completion of the secondary survey may be required for bleeding that cannot be controlled in the Emergency Department … Inserting a chest drain into a massive haemothorax may improve ventilation but stopping ongoing bleeding can only be done in theatre
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - primary survey' (Last Updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Major_paediatric_trauma_The_primary_survey/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Any impairment on AVPU → formal GCS.** Check pupils, movement in all four limbs, and **blood glucose on arrival.**
claims.source_text: Any impairment on AVPU scale should prompt a formal assessment of GCS … Check pupil response to light … Check movement in all four limbs … Measure blood glucose level on arrival
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - primary survey' (Last Updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Major_paediatric_trauma_The_primary_survey/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Prevent secondary brain injury:** keep oxygenation adequate, correct hypotension and hypoglycaemia, nurse head-up 30 degrees. Consider urgent CT brain and neurosurgical discussion.
claims.source_text: Avoid secondary brain injury by: maintaining adequate oxygenation correcting hypotension nursing head up to 30 degrees correcting hypoglycaemia … Consider need for urgent CT brain and discussion with neurosurgery
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - primary survey' (Last Updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Major_paediatric_trauma_The_primary_survey/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Expose to find life-threatening injuries, but prevent hypothermia** — limit exposure and warm all ongoing fluids.
claims.source_text: Remove clothing and look for any obvious life-threatening injury … Avoid hypothermia by limiting exposure and by warming all ongoing fluids
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - primary survey' (Last Updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Major_paediatric_trauma_The_primary_survey/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **All children with major trauma should be transferred to a major trauma service** for definitive care, following local pre-hospital and inter-hospital transfer guidelines.
claims.source_text: All children with major trauma should be transferred to a major trauma service for definitive management. This should be done in consultation with the local pre-hospital and inter-hospital transfer guidelines
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Trauma - primary survey' (Last Updated January 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Major_paediatric_trauma_The_primary_survey/, retrieved 2026-09-23
